name: CT Hackerspace
summary: Closed. A 4,000 sq ft volunteer-run hackerspace in Watertown, for years the oldest in Connecticut. Its website was still live and current-looking after it shut.

operations.hours_note: Free public open night every Wednesday 7–10pm — tours, and visitors may use tools at no cost.

equipment.notes: 4×8 ft cutting area, plus a 4×4 in CNC engraver
Milling machine with DRO, large metal lathe, metal shaper, power hacksaw, arbor press, media blast cabinet
Radial arm saw, table saw, band saw, belt and spindle sanders, scroll saw
Soldering stations, oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, dedicated Arduino station

sources.note: 'CT Makerspaces Map' attached to the superseded Google Site. This record is the 'CT Hackerspace' pin and nothing else — the pin carried a name and a location, no other detail.
Own site: 30 Echo Lake Road, Watertown CT 06795; a 4,000 sq ft space; free public open night Wednesdays 7–10pm; phone (804) 601-4225.
Independently listed as CT Hackerspace, Watertown — corroborating that the map pin recovered from the old site is a currently operating space.

Own equipment page, transcribed: Lulzbot Mini; Universal Laser Systems M300 50W CO2; CNC wood router (4×8 ft) and CNC engraver; Bridgeport mill with DRO, large metal lathe, metal shaper, power hacksaw; table saw, band saw, radial arm saw, sanders, scroll saw; electronics bench and Arduino station; small lathe for pen turning.

Regional steward (MakeHaven) reports the space has closed. Recorded on the steward's word against a still-live website — cthacker.space was serving an ordinary, current-looking site with a weekly open night on it days before this, and carried no closure notice.

gaps: whether the equipment was dispersed, sold or moved to another space is unknown
the equipment and address below describe the space as it operated, not as it is now
